timings.notes: Grand Brahmotsavam in Panguni

moolavar.name: Venkatakrishnan (Parthasarathy)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, with moustache showing the charioteer aspect

triplicane.puranam: Krishna here serves as Parthasarathy, the charioteer of Arjuna in the Kurukshetra war; the Moolavar still bears the marks of Bhishma’s arrows, and he refused to take up weapons, honouring his vow.

pasuram.meaning: Thirumangai Azhwar hails the Lord of Thiruvallikkeni who bore the Pandavas’ burden as their charioteer.

timings.notes: Hill shrine has steps — darshan by climb

moolavar.name: Neervannan
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing at the hill shrine

thiruneermalai.puranam: Thirumangai Azhwar waited six months at this water-hill for darshan; the Lord then revealed himself to him in four forms — standing, seated, reclining and walking.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar sings of Neervannan of the sacred hill surrounded by holy waters.

timings.notes: Athi Varadar rises from the Anantha Saras tank once in 40 years

moolavar.name: Varadharaja (Devaraja)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing on the Athigiri hill

kanchi-varadaraja.puranam: Brahma worshipped the Lord at the Athigiri hill here; the Athi Varadar image, carved from the heartwood of an athi fig tree, emerges from the temple tank every forty years in a festival drawing millions.

pasuram.meaning: Long live Kanchi, long live the jewel-hued Lord of Hastigiri — those who praise him find their days and lives ever flourishing.
pasuram.tamil: வாழியே கச்சி வாழியே ஹஸ்திகிரி மணிவண்ணன் வாழ்த்துவார் வாழ்வும் நாளும் வளர்ந்தோங்கும்
pasuram.transliteration: Vaazhiye Kacchi vaazhiye Hasthigiri manivannan — vaazhththuvaar vaazhvum naalum valarngaum

thiruvekka.puranam: When the haughty Saraswati tried to drown the area with the Vegavati river in flood, the Lord lay down as a dam across her course — and when Thirumazhisai Azhwar commanded, he rolled up like a mat and followed his devotee out of Kanchi.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who did exactly as his devotee said — "sonna vannam seitha" — earning this kshetram its name.

moolavar.name: Aadhikesava (Ashtabhuja Perumal)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing with eight arms holding eight weapons

ashtabujam.puranam: Gajendra the elephant king worshipped here; the Lord appeared with eight arms to shelter him, a form he keeps to this day.

pasuram.meaning: The eight-armed Lord of Thiru Ashtabujam who wields the conch, discus, bow and mace together.

timings.notes: Part of the single Ulagalantha Perumal complex

moolavar.name: Ulagalantha Perumal (Trivikrama)
moolavar.form: Nindran — the giant form of Vamana’s third stride

thiruooragam.puranam: Mahabali, humbled by Vamana’s three strides that measured all the worlds, is said to hold the Lord’s raised foot here even now — Adisesha (Ooragam) himself forms the shrine’s serpent legend.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar worships the one who measured the three worlds yet rests tiny in the devotee’s heart.

timings.notes: Shrine within the Ulagalantha Perumal complex

thiruneeragam.puranam: The water-principle (neer) of the sacred deluge is worshipped here — the Lord who preserved the waters of creation within the Ulagalantha complex.

pasuram.meaning: Praise to Neeragathan, the Lord of the holy waters of Kanchi.

timings.notes: Shrine within the Ulagalantha Perumal complex

thirukkaragam.puranam: The Lord here is the very ocean of mercy — Karunakaran — who receives the worship once offered by the celestials at Kanchi.

pasuram.meaning: The merciful Lord of Kaaragam who forgives every failing of the devotee.

timings.notes: Shrine within the Ulagalantha Perumal complex

thirukkarvanam.puranam: The rain-cloud hue of the Lord here is worshipped as the giver of the season’s rains to the groves of Kanchi.

pasuram.meaning: The cloud-hued Lord of Kaarvaanam who showers grace like the first rain.

timings.notes: Pallava-era structure

moolavar.name: Vaikundanathan
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated, with reclining and standing forms on the upper tiers

parameswara-vinnagaram.puranam: Built by the Pallava king Nandivarman II, whose coronation the Lord is said to have blessed; the three-tier sanctum shows him seated, reclining and standing.

pasuram.meaning: The seated Lord of Parameswara Vinnagaram, the Paramapada that grants moksha.

pavalavannam.puranam: The coral-hued Lord emerged from the sacrificial fire of the sages here, glowing like polished ruby (pavalam).

pasuram.meaning: The ruby-hued Lord of Thiruppaavalavannam who glows in the devotee’s heart.

moolavar.name: Pandava Thoodhar (Krishna)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated in the giant vishvaroopa form of the divine messenger

thiruppadagam.puranam: Krishna came as the Pandavas’ messenger (thoodhar) to Duryodhana’s court; here he reveals that towering vishvaroopa form, seated in majesty.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar marvels that the Lord who measured worlds consented to serve as a messenger.

timings.notes: Within the Ekambaranathar temple complex

nilathingal-thundam.puranam: Within Shiva’s Ekambaranathar temple, Vishnu is worshipped as the cool quarter of the moon that once cooled the burning serpent-fire of Kanchi’s legend.

pasuram.meaning: The moon-hued Lord within the ancient Ekambara grove.

timings.notes: Within the Kamakshi Amman temple complex

thirukkalvanoor.puranam: The primordial Varaha shrine stands behind the Kamakshi Amman sanctum — the "Kalvan" (divine thief) who steals the devotee’s heart with his glance.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of Kalvanoor who takes the devotee’s heart as his own dwelling.

thiruvelukkai.puranam: Narasimha, still blazing after Hiranya’s end, was cooled by the prayer of the celestials here and seated himself in serene yoga — the beautiful lion of the Velukkai grove.

pasuram.meaning: The fierce-yet-graceful Lord of Velukkai who guards Kanchi in seated yoga.

thiruthanka.puranam: When Saraswati’s darkness swallowed Kanchi, the Lord appeared as the lamp of all light (deepa prakasa) that ended the age of delusion — the shrine of Poigai Azhwar’s first lamp-verse.

pasuram.meaning: With the world as the lamp, the seas as the ghee, and the blazing sun as its flame, the Azhwar lit his first lamp of devotion — at this kshetram of the lamp-lord.
pasuram.tamil: வையம் தகளியா வார்கடலே நெய்யாக வையக் கதிரோன் விளக்கென வித்தது சுடரே
pasuram.transliteration: Vaiyam thagaliyaa vaarkadalai neyyaaga vaiyak kadhiron vilakkena viththadhu sudare

thiruputkuzhi.puranam: Rama performed the burial of the eagle Jatayu here, digging the pit (putkuzhi) with his own hands — the shrine of his compassion for a fallen devotee.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of Putkuzhi who gave even a bird the honour of a devotee’s passing.

timings.notes: Known as Vaidya Veeraraghava — prayers for healing

moolavar.name: Vaidya Veeraraghava
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining, right hand raised in healing

tiruvallur.puranam: Salihotra the sage offered his devotion in a leech-infested tank here; the Lord rose as a wounded old man whom the sage tended — and healed him, earning the name Vaidya, the divine physician of Tiruvallur.

pasuram.meaning: The healer of Tiruvallur who cures the illness of samsara itself.

thirunindravur.puranam: On his way to Venkatam, the Lord was stopped by his devotee’s devotion and stayed — "nindraan" — at this village; the Thaayar here is called "Ennai Petra Thaayar", the mother who holds her children.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who stood still for love of his devotee at Thirunindravur.

timings.notes: Popular for marriage blessings

moolavar.name: Nithyakalyana (Aadalmaiyappan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing with Bhoomidevi on his shoulder

thiruvidanthai.puranam: The Lord of the shore married 360 maidens of the fishermen’s folk in a single year and held them all as one in his form — ever- wed (nithya kalyana) for the sake of his devotees.

pasuram.meaning: The ever-wed Lord of Vidandai by the Kadal-mallai shore.

moolavar.name: Sthala Sayana Perumal
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining on the shore floor

mahabalipuram.puranam: Praised as the birthplace of Bhoothathazhwar, this shore-shrine is where a devotee-king learned that the Lord rests wherever his devotee rests — and so he reclines by the sea itself.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar born at Kadalmallai sings of the Lord who reclines amid the sounding waves.

timings.notes: Yoga Anjaneyar hill shrine nearby

moolavar.name: Yoga Narasimha (Akkarakani)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated in yoga on the hill

sholinghur.puranam: Seven eternal rishis are said to be in meditation on this hill since ages past; Narasimha sits in yoga here, the wish-granting gem (akkarakani) of the devotees.

pasuram.meaning: The yoga-seated Narasimha of Kadigai, where even a moment of devotion bears endless fruit.

timings.notes: Vishwaroopa darshan 06:15–07:00; Ekadasi special

moolavar.name: Ranganathan (Nam Perumal)
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining on Adisesha, facing south

srirangam.puranam: Rama gifted Vibhishana this image of Ranganatha as he returned to Lanka; set down at the Kaveri island it took root there — the self-manifested first among the 108, sung by eleven Azhwars and the seat of the Sri Vaishnava lineage.

pasuram.meaning: Awake, O Lord of Srirangam — waken from your rest amid the glowing lamps and the sweet music of your devotees.
pasuram.tamil: பாயும் ஒளி விளக்கும் பத்தருள் திருப்பள்ளியெழுச்சி பாயும் பொன் விளக்கும் பண்மொழியால் பள்ளியெழுந்தருளாயே
pasuram.transliteration: Paayum oli vilakkum paththarul thiruppalliyezhuchchi — paayum pon vilakkum pannmozhiaal palliyezhundharulaaye

timings.notes: Goddess-led temple — Nachiyar receives first honours

uraiyur.puranam: A Chola princess’s devotion won the Lord himself as bridegroom here; to this day the Nachiyar leads all processions and first honours, for the groom came to her city.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar hails the wedding-lord of ancient Uraiyur, the Chola capital.

timings.notes: Shiva, Brahma and Vishnu worshipped together here

uthamar-kovil.puranam: Brahma’s lost worship was restored here; the unique shrine holds Vishnu as Purushothaman with Shiva and Brahma beside him — the Trimurti in one courtyard.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar serves the Lord of Karambanoor where all three gods stand together.

timings.notes: White hill (vellai — white); Marutha vahanam festival

thiruvellarai.puranam: The white hill of Thiruvellarai is said to be older than Srirangam itself; sage Markandeya worshipped the lotus-eyed (Pundarikaksha) Lord here, and the temple’s Persian-style entrance towers are unique in Tamil Nadu.

pasuram.meaning: The lotus-eyed Lord of the white hill who receives the first Azhwar’s praise.

anbil.puranam: Sage Valmiki is said to have worshipped here; the beautiful (vadhivazhagiya) Lord reclines facing the Kollidam’s flowing waters at Anbil.

pasuram.meaning: Thirumazhisai’s verse embraces the reclining beauty of Anbil.

timings.notes: On the Kollidam south bank

koviladi.puranam: Emperor Sibhi, who gave his own flesh to save a dove, received the Lord’s grace here; the Lord reclines holding the pot of appam — the offering that fed the sage Upamanyu.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar numbers Thiruppernagar among the shrines that carry the soul across the flood.

kandiyur.puranam: Brahma’s severed head clung to Shiva’s palm until his curse was undone here — the Lord freed Shiva from the "hara sabha" of sin at Kandiyur, beside the Shiva temple where Brahma is also worshipped.

pasuram.meaning: The liberator at Kandiyur who frees even the gods from their curses.

thiruvelliyangudi.puranam: Garuda performed penance here and the Lord appeared with the bow of Rama — the rare kshetram where Garuda is honoured as guru, worshipped in a separate sanctum.

pasuram.meaning: The bow-bearing Rama of Velliyangudi who blesses through his eagle-lord.

aadanoor.puranam: Here the Lord keeps the wheel of time — "aandu alakkum", he who measures the year — reclining with his consorts upon the serpent couch.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who rules the turning year from Aadanoor’s sanctum.

timings.notes: Famous chariot festival (Chithirai)

moolavar.name: Aravamudhan (Sarangapani)
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining in the vaulted chariot-shaped sanctum (uthanga sayana)

kumbakonam.puranam: When Thirumazhisai Azhwar rose to leave Kumbakonam in sorrow, the Lord began to follow him, half-risen from his couch — and remains in that half-rising posture, the sweet nectar (aravamudhu) of the Kaveri delta.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who lies in sweet Kudanthai — seeing him, even the proud fall in swoon of wonder, brighter than lightning to the eye.
pasuram.tamil: இடவாழி வண்குடந்தை கிடந்தான் கைதொழக் கண்டகால் கதிரொன்றின் மின்னியதன் மடியிலார்
pasuram.transliteration: Idavaazhi vankudanthai kidandhaan kai thozhak kandakaal — kadhironrin minniyadhan madiyilaar

pullamboothangudi.puranam: Rama’s bow-skilled form (val vil) rests here; the kshetram is linked to the legend of Jatayu’s kin and the consolation Rama granted the birds of the Pullabhudangudi grove.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar dwells on the reclining Rama of Pullabhudangudi who grants the deepest wishes.

moolavar.name: Gajendra Varadhan
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, discus raised for Gajendra

kabisthalam.puranam: The elephant-king Gajendra’s cry of surrender was answered here in an instant — Gajendra Varadha is the emblem of the Lord who runs to the helpless devotee without awaiting perfection.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who flew to the elephant’s rescue at Kapisthalam.

thirunandhipuram.puranam: The bull (nandhi) of Shiva is said to have turned to worship Vishnu here — hence Nandhipura Vinnagaram, where worshipping once is held to equal the fruit of many pilgrimages.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of Nandhipura, greater than the distant grandeur of other shrines.

thirukkoodalur.puranam: The gathered (koodal) celestials took shelter of the Lord here when Indra’s elephant was seized — Jagathrakshakan, protector of worlds, stands guard at Koodalur.

pasuram.meaning: The protector of Koodalur who shields all who gather under his feet.

timings.notes: Temple kitchen cooks without salt — Prasadam tradition

moolavar.name: Oppilliappan (Uppiliappan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, hand raised in precept (upadesa)

uppiliappan.puranam: The Lord wooed Bhoomidevi in a sage’s hermitage here insisting every dish be salt-free — "uppu illa appan" — symbolising that he accepts our offering however imperfect, as a groom accepts the bride’s people.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar’s bridal longing — the soul’s wedding to the Lord of Thiruvinnagar.

timings.notes: Nachiyar leads all processions — only temple where the Goddess is honoured first

nachiyar-kovil.puranam: Vanjulavalli, a sage’s daughter, won the Lord as her groom — he granted that she would lead in every honour forever; the temple’s stone chariot (kal garudan) is famed for growing in weight as it is pulled.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar serves the Nambi of Naraiyur where the Goddess leads and the Lord follows her honour.

timings.notes: Sara nathan — with five consorts

thirucherai.puranam: At the deluge’s end, the Lord alone received the seeds of creation and the Vedas for safekeeping — Saranathan, the refuge; the sage Kasyapa’s five wives serve him here as his five consorts.

pasuram.meaning: The refuge of Thirucherai who carries the soul through every dissolution.

timings.notes: Famed Abhishekam; bee-mandapa (vanamali) legend

thirukkannamangai.puranam: The Goddess herself performed penance here with a thousand lotuses; when one fell short she offered her own eye — the Lord holds her as Abhishegavalli, and bees are said to hum her hymn in the mandapa to this day.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar lingers at Kannamangai where the Goddess’s devotion won the Lord’s tenderness.

timings.notes: Three shrines — Neelamegha, Manikundram, Narasimha

thanjai-mamanikoil.puranam: The three Thanjavur shrines — Neelamegha Perumal, Manikundram and Yoga Narasimha — are counted as one Divya Desam; the demon Tanjan was felled here and the city took his name with the Lord’s blessing.

pasuram.meaning: All the Thirumangai verses for Thanjai embrace its three shrines together as one holy place.

thiruvazhundur.puranam: Krishna grazed his cows at this grove (aamaruvi — the cowherd’s Lord); the sage Vedadasa’s devotion here drew the Lord’s promise that his name would echo as the Deva’s king.

pasuram.meaning: The cowherd-king of Thiruvazhundur whose groves echoed with Krishna’s flute.

thiruchirupuliyur.puranam: Vyagrapada the tiger-footed sage’s devotion here made the Lord an ocean of grace (arul maakadal); worshipped also as Kripasamudra, the sea of compassion.

pasuram.meaning: The ocean of grace at Chirupuliyur whose depth no hymn can sound.

thalaichangadu.puranam: The sun and the moon (nan madhi) are said to worship the Lord here at the delta’s head (thalai) — the village gifted a divine conch to the Chola king’s devotion.

pasuram.meaning: The first-shrine Lord of Thalaichangadu whom sun and moon alike serve.

moolavar.name: Parimala Ranganatha
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining with head to the south

thiruindalur.puranam: The fragrant (parimala) Ranganatha reclines on the Cauvery’s north bank at Mayiladuthurai; the river herself is said to worship him here as she turns to the sea.

pasuram.meaning: The fragrance of the Lord of Indaloor that fills the devotee’s heart like garlands of the river.

timings.notes: Famous for the "Sowrirajan" never-shaven tirtha tradition

thirukkannapuram.puranam: A devotee-priest’s faith was answered when the Lord revealed a tuft (sowri) of hair he was said not to have — Sowrirajan, whose word alone is enough; the "Muthukulitha" thirumeni here is famed for instant grace.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar’s decad sings the Lord of Kannapuram whose mere word is the devotee’s rescue.

thirukkannangudi.puranam: Krishna, the butter-thief (Damodara), lingered here for the love of a devotee’s offering — the playful Lord of Kannangudi whose charm the Azhwar likens to his cowherd days.

pasuram.meaning: The Damodara of Kannangudi who lets himself be caught by devotion alone.

nagapattinam.puranam: The beautiful (soundara) Lord of the coastal city of Nagai, whose royal bearing Thirumangai Azhwar describes as beyond the three worlds’ wealth.

pasuram.meaning: The beautiful king of Thirunaagai whose beauty outshines every treasure.

timings.notes: Within the Nataraja temple complex — Chitsabha darshan

moolavar.name: Govindaraja
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining, facing east, beside the Chitsabha

chidambaram.puranam: At the cosmic dance-floor of Thillai, Vishnu reclines as Govindaraja in the same hall where Shiva dances — the two-fold vision of the One; the shrine was restored under Akbar’s era after long disputes.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar bows to the reclining Lord of Thillai’s golden hall.

sirkazhi.puranam: In the Kazheesirama Vinnagaram of Sirkazhi, the Lord who strode the three worlds is worshipped; the town is also the birthplace of the child-wonder Thirugnanasambandar, whose meeting with Thirumangai Azhwar here is legend.

pasuram.meaning: The three-world measurer of Kazheesirama Vinnagaram, praised as "Mann alantha thadalan".

timings.notes: Twin villages counted as one Desam

thiruvali-thirunagari.puranam: The pacified Lakshmi Narasimha of Thiruvaali and the Devaraja of Thirunagari — Mahabali is said to worship here as King of the Naga lords; the two villages’ shrines are honoured together in every hymn.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar sings the paired glory of Thiruvaali and Thirunagari where Narasimha rests in peace.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

thirukavalambadi.puranam: The cowherd Krishna of the Kavalan-grove — one of the eleven Thirunangur forms that rose when Shiva danced.

pasuram.meaning: The cowherd lord of Kavalambadi whose flute still calls the devotee.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

arimeya-vinnagaram.puranam: When Shiva danced with the pot, the Lord appeared here as Kudamudakoothan — the pot-dancer — in his seat at Arimeya Vinnagaram.

pasuram.meaning: The pot-dance lord of Arimeya Vinnagaram amid the Thirunangur eleven.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

vanpurushothamam.puranam: The supreme Purusha of the Thirunangur grove — worshipped as the first among beings at Vanpurushothamam.

pasuram.meaning: The primal Purusha of Thiruvanpurushothamam who precedes all creation.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

semponseikoil.puranam: Rama is said to have worshipped here with gold for Jatayu’s rites — the golden (sempon) shrine of Perarulaalan, the great-graceful one.

pasuram.meaning: The great-graceful Lord of Semponseikoil who crowns the humblest offering.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

manimadakoil.puranam: The jewel-pavilion (mani madam) temple where the seated Lord grants audience to the Thirunangur devotee as a king to his court.

pasuram.meaning: The seated king of Manimadakoil who receives the devotee as his own.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group; Garuda seva festival

vaikunta-vinnagaram.puranam: Vaikunta on earth among the Thirunangur eleven — all eleven deities ride together in the famed Garuda seva festival that draws the delta’s faithful.

pasuram.meaning: The Vaikuntanathan of Thirunangur who brings heaven to the Kaveri’s sands.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

devanartogai.puranam: Where the assembled (thogai) Devas worshipped — Deivanayagan, leader of the celestial host, among the eleven of Thirunangur.

pasuram.meaning: The lord of the assembled Devas at Thirudevanartogai.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

thetriyambalam.puranam: The red-hued (segnmaal) Ranganatha who reclines eternally at Thiruthetriyambalam — the shrine of vows within the Thirunangur ring.

pasuram.meaning: The reclining red-hued Lord of Thetriyambalam who never abandons his vow to the devotee.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

manikkoodam.puranam: The boon-giver of the jewel-court (mani koodam) — Varadharajan among the Thirunangur eleven.

pasuram.meaning: The boon-giving Varadharaja of Manikkoodam.

timings.notes: Annan Kovil — "elder brother of Venkatam"

vellakulam.puranam: The white-tank shrine honoured as the elder brother (annan) of Tirupati Srinivasa — worshipping here is held to bear the fruit of the Seven Hills.

pasuram.meaning: The elder-brother Srinivasa of Vellakulam, equal to Venkatam’s Lord.

timings.notes: Thirunangur group

parthanpalli.puranam: Arjuna (Parthan) worshipped here after the war’s grief; the Lord who belongs to the lotus-eyed (thamaraiyal kelvan) received his offering at Parthanpalli.

pasuram.meaning: Poigai Azhwar’s verse for the lotus-eyed one’s lord at Parthanpalli.

thiruvahindrapuram.puranam: Adisesha himself bore this hill (Oushadagiri) so its healing herbs could serve the world; Indra’s worship made the Lord its Deivanathan, and the great acharya Vedanta Desika — born near here — poured his hymns on the Lord of the hill.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar’s decad for Deivanathan of the serpent-borne healing hill.

thirukkovilur.puranam: The first three Azhwars — Poigai, Bhoothath and Pey — met by chance in a pilgrim’s narrow shelter here on a stormy night, and their three lamps of devotion lit the first Tamil hymns of the Prabandham at this Vamana kshetram.

pasuram.meaning: The mudhal Azhwars’ meeting at Thirukkovilur kindled the first verses of Tamil devotion.

timings.notes: Five forms of the Lord worshipped in one complex

thirukkurungudi.puranam: The Lord himself came as a disciple to Vaishnava teachers here, learning the sacred texts at their feet — Nambi of Kurungudi, at the Mahendragiri foothills, who appears in five forms across the village.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar’s bridal verses for the Nambi of Kurungudi who accepts the soul as his own.

timings.notes: Eternal lamp (nondi vilakku) tradition

nanguneri.puranam: The banyan (vanamamalai) of the celestials shaded this seat of the Lord; the great lamp of Nanguneri, tended by the Vanamamalai mutt lineage, has burned without cease for centuries.

pasuram.meaning: The ever-lit Lord of Thiruvaraamangai whom the Vedas themselves praise without end.

timings.notes: Birthplace of Nammazhwar; Garuda seva in Vaikasi

moolavar.name: Aadhinathan (Polindu Nindra Piran)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing under the aged tamarind tree

alwar-thirunagari.puranam: The tamarind tree here neither sleeps nor bears sour fruit, legend says, since Nammazhwar sat beneath it in unbroken meditation from his birth; the Lord served as his teacher and the village became the holiest seat of the Prabandham.

pasuram.meaning: In his own hymns Nammazhwar sings the Lord of his birth-grove who taught him all wisdom.

moolavar.name: Vaithamanidhi Perumal
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining with arm as pillow

thirukkolur.puranam: Kubera’s treasury (maanidhi) was kept here; a maid’s innocent complaint — "I brought nothing and gained nothing" — became the Lord’s teaching of surrender, and he stays as the stored-treasure of the helpless.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of Kolur who owns every treasure yet asks only the devotee’s heart.

thirupperai.puranam: Bhoomidevi’s prayer won the Lord’s heart here; his earrings shaped like the fish (makara) of the deep are praised by Nammazhwar, and the Thaayar’s beloved (kuzhai kaadhal) form gives the temple its name.

pasuram.meaning: The fish-eared beauty of Thirupperai whose glance itself is the ornament of the soul.

timings.notes: Nava Thirupathi group on the Thamirabarani

srivaikuntam.puranam: The Lord hid as a thief (kallar piran) to protect the celestials’ treasury from the demon here — Vaikunta on earth along the Thamirabarani’s banks, first of the Nava Thirupathi nine.

pasuram.meaning: The Vaikuntanathan of Srivaikuntam who guards his devotees’ wealth of devotion.

timings.notes: Nava Thirupathi group

thirukkulandai.puranam: At Perungulam’s great tank the Lord appeared to the sage Eeswarapaadar’s devotion; Kulandai — the beloved child of the Thamirabarani country — Srinivasa of Thirukkulandai.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of the kulam (tank) village who is himself the child-treasure of the devout.

timings.notes: Nava Thirupathi group

thiruvaragunamangai.puranam: The Lord sat here in victory (vijaya asana) after subduing the demon who seized the Vedas — second darshan of the Nava Thirupathi by the Natham lake.

pasuram.meaning: The victory-seated Lord of Varagunamangai who wins the devotee’s inner battles.

timings.notes: Nava Thirupathi group

thiruppuliangudi.puranam: The king who burned (kaichina) with the fire of devotion — Kaisina Vendhan of the palmyra (puli) grove, one of the Nava Thirupathi nine.

pasuram.meaning: The flame-like king of Thiruppuliangudi whose glow is the devotee’s guide.

timings.notes: Twin shrines (Irattai Thirupathi) — count as one Desam

tholaivillimangalam.puranam: Two shrines — Devapiran and Aravindalochanan — stand on the two banks of the dry riverbed and are worshipped together as the "twin birthplace" (Irattai Thirupathi) of the Nava Thirupathi.

pasuram.meaning: The lotus-eyed twin lords of Tholaivillimangalam whom one hymn embraces both at once.

thiruthangal.puranam: The Lord stood (nindraan) here awaiting Sridevi’s penance’s fruit at the hill of Thiruthangal — the town where Thirumangai Azhwar’s verses settled like a lamp in the Pandya country.

pasuram.meaning: The standing Narayana of Thiruthangal who waits upon his devotee’s longing.

timings.notes: Temple tower is the emblem of Tamil Nadu; Aadi Puram festival

moolavar.name: Vatapatrasayi (Vatapatrasayee)
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining on the banyan leaf

srivilliputhur.puranam: Periyazhwar found the divine child Andal beneath the tulsi here; her Thiruppavai and her wedding into the Lord’s shrine made Srivilliputhur the home of the only woman Azhwar — the town’s tower flies on Tamil Nadu’s seal.

pasuram.meaning: O maidens of the cowherd town — the moonlit month of Margazhi has dawned; come, let us bathe in the vow of the dawn.
pasuram.tamil: மார்கழித் திங்கள் மதிநிறந்தண்ணால் நீராடப் போதுவீர் போதுமினோ நேரிழையீர்
pasuram.transliteration: Maargazhi thingal madhiniRandhu nannaal neeraada podhuveer — podhumino neraizhaiyeer

timings.notes: Three postures in three tiers — standing, seated, reclining

moolavar.name: Koodal Azhagar (Vyamooga Perumal)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, with seated and reclining forms above

madurai-koodal.puranam: At Madurai’s sangam (koodal) of rivers and scholars, the Azhagar shows three postures in one sanctum-tower — standing, seated and reclining — meeting the devotee at every height of devotion.

pasuram.meaning: Periyazhwar, born in this city, sings the beautiful Lord of Koodal’s confluence.

timings.notes: Chithirai festival — Azhagar rides to the Vaigai

moolavar.name: Kallazhagar (Maayon)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, in the fragrant forest shrine

thirumaliruncholai.puranam: The beautiful lord of the Alagar hills rides the golden horse to Madurai each Chithirai, halting mid-river at the Vaigai — the beloved Azhagar of the Tamil country’s greatest festival, keeping his word though late.

pasuram.meaning: Periyazhwar’s verses sing the deep groves of Maalirunscholai where the dark Lord grazes his devotees like calves.

timings.notes: Celebrated Chakrathalvar shrine with 154 hands

thirumogur.puranam: The Devas sought the nectar here; the Lord appeared as the dark cloud (kala megam) of grace, and his Sudarshana at Mogur — the sixteen-armed, 154-handed Chakrathalvar — is the most celebrated weapon-shrine in the south.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar’s decad hails the cloud-hued Lord of Mogur who rained nectar on the Devas.

timings.notes: Darbasayana — Rama reclines on darba grass

thirupullani.puranam: Rama lay on darba grass for three nights here, eyes fixed on the sea, until the ocean-lord surrendered — the kshetram of unwavering resolve, where Vibhishana too found refuge at the shore-shrine of Kothandam.

pasuram.meaning: Kulasekhara longs to serve the setu-shore of Pullani where Rama lay resolved upon the sea.

timings.notes: Ashtakshara kshetram — Ramanuja proclaimed the sacred mantra here

moolavar.name: Sowmya Narayana (Uraga Mellanayaan)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated (ashtanga vimana), with reclining and standing forms above

thirukkoshtiyur.puranam: Defying his guru’s threat of hell, Ramanuja climbed this temple’s tiered vimana and proclaimed the Ashtakshara mantra to all the world — "join me at Koshtiyur and be saved"; the three-tier sanctum holds the Lord seated, reclining and standing.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar serves the three-formed Lord of Koshtiyur who holds the assembly of devotees in his heart.

timings.notes: Rock-cut cave shrines of the Pallava-Pandya era

moolavar.name: Sathyagiri Nathan (Sathyamurthi)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing; giant rock-cut Anantasayana beside

thirumeyyam.puranam: On the hill of truth (mey — sathya) the Pandya king cut the Lord from living rock: the vast reclining Anantasayana carved in a single cave remains among the largest rock-cut Vishnus in India.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of the truth-hill at Meyyam who keeps his word to the rock-steady devotee.

timings.notes: Darshan through three doors; Arattu festival of the royal family

moolavar.name: Anantha Padmanabha (Panguni Naayakan)
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining through three doors (Siva, Vishnu, Brahma aspects)

thiruvananthapuram.puranam: A sage-child (Vilvamangalathu Swamiyar) heard the Lord as a mischievous boy and chased him into an ilinja tree that split to reveal the reclining colossus — Padmanabha of the Anantha hills, whose vaults made the shrine famed as the richest temple on earth.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar sings the Lord of Malayala’s hills who reclines at Thiruvananthapuram in eternal ease.

moolavar.name: Thiruvazhmarban (Kuralappan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, Lakshmi at his chest

thiruvanparisaram.puranam: The Lord whose chest (marbu) bears Lakshmi (thiru) — the Nanjil country’s refuge, where Nathamuni’s lineage and the Cherakolloor kings worshipped in turn.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who carries Lakshmi at his heart, ruling the Parisaram grove.

timings.notes: Onam festival origin shrine

moolavar.name: Vamana (Kaatkarai Appan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing in the dwarf-brahmin form

thirukkatkarai.puranam: Mahabali’s kingdom covered Kerala when Vamana asked for three paces of land here — the Onam festival itself is this kshetram’s celebration, with the Onathappan image worshipped in every home of Kerala.

pasuram.meaning: The Vamana of Kaatkarai who measured worlds for love of a devotee’s word.

moolavar.name: Moozhikkalathan (Srikantan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, with Lakshmana and Bharata beside

thirumoozhikkalam.puranam: Sage Hema’s penance here was answered when the Lord spoke sweet wisdom (moozhikkai — the counsel of the mantra); Rama’s brothers stand with him in this Rama-shrine of Kerala.

pasuram.meaning: The counsel-giving Lord of Moozhikkalam who guides the seeker’s questions.

timings.notes: One of the five Vishnu shrines of Chengannur

thiruppuliyur.puranam: Sage Pundareeka’s tapas at the tiger-grove (puli) drew the wonder-working (maaya) Lord here — Puliyur of the Pamba’s banks.

pasuram.meaning: The wonder-lord of Thiruppuliyur whom the Azhwar holds as his own child.

thiruchengundrur.puranam: Even the Himalaya’s lord (imayavarappan) worshipped here — Yudhishthira is said to have consecrated this shrine after the war, in the red-hill (chengunroor) town by the Pamba.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord whom even the mountains worship, seated in Chengunroor’s heart.

timings.notes: Bharathapuzha bali-rituals for ancestors

thirunavai.puranam: Nine yogis (navamukundam) were freed from a serpent-curse by the Lord’s grace at this Bharathapuzha ghat — Kerala’s holiest ground for the ancestor-rites performed on its banks.

pasuram.meaning: The nine-sage Lord of Thirunavai who frees every lineage that remembers him.

timings.notes: Garuda icon in seated worship; stone flag-post unique in Kerala

thiruvalla.puranam: Durvasa’s disciple was saved here by the Lord’s grace and the mighty Garuda himself is worshipped in a seated shrine — the black-stone flagpost of Thiruvalla has stood sentinel over the Vallabha shrine for a thousand years.

pasuram.meaning: The Kolapiran of Thiruvalla whom Garuda serves with folded wings.

moolavar.name: Paambanaiyappan (Kamalanathan)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing on the serpent couch

thiruvanvandoor.puranam: The legendary architect Perunchithiranar built this shrine overnight for the serpent-couch (paambanai) Lord — one of the five Pamba-river Vishnu temples.

pasuram.meaning: The serpent-couch lord of Vanvandoor whose rest sustains the worlds.

timings.notes: Aranmula boat-race (Uthrattathi Vallamkali) and kannadi (metal mirror) traditions

thiruvaranvilai.puranam: Arjuna is said to have raised this shrine in thanks after his pilgrimage; the sacred boat-race escorts the Lord’s offerings down the Pamba, and Aranmula’s metal mirrors were born of a temple-work accident of the-visvakarma guilds.

pasuram.meaning: The lovely Kannan of Aranmula whom the river carries garlands of song.

timings.notes: Metal-inlaid reclining image; Otraikkadal mandapam

moolavar.name: Aadhikesava Perumal
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining, head to the west

thiruvattaru.puranam: Between the rivers Para and Thaayar, the Lord reclines on Adisesha in a sanctum of metal-inlaid stone; Hanuman is said to guard him facing south — the great Adikesava of the old Travancore country.

pasuram.meaning: The primal Kesava of Thiruvattaru whom the twin rivers worship on either bank.

thiruvithuvakodu.puranam: The refuge-giver (abhaya pradan) of Thiruvithuvakkodu grants the devotee freedom from fear — Bilvamangala’s longing verses found their answer in this Palakkad grove.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord of Vithuvakkodu who carries the soul across (uyya) the ocean of birth.

thirukkodithanam.puranam: Sahadeva of the Pandavas planted the temple flag (kodi) here in penance — the flag-shrine (kodi sthanam) where Amrithanathan grants the nectar of devotion.

pasuram.meaning: The wonder (athbudha) Narayana of Kodithanam who sweetens the devotee’s path.

timings.notes: Sarva darshan queues nearly continuous; check TTD for current schedule

moolavar.name: Srinivasa (Venkateswara, Balaji)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, self-manifested on the Venkata hill

tirupati.puranam: In this age the Lord of the Seven Hills grants kalyana-proti worship as in no other shrine — Vishnu who came down as Srinivasa to wed Padmavathi remains on Venkatam until the end of the age, the debt of devotion paid in darshans by millions.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar refuses every other refuge, clinging to the Lord of Venkatam who holds the mountain and the hill of the soul.

timings.notes: Nine shrines spread through forest — Upper Ahobilam needs a trek

moolavar.name: Nava Narasimha (Ahobila Narasimha)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated, nine forms across the Nallamala forest

ahobilam.puranam: Where the pillar of Hiranya’s palace split and Narasimha burst forth — the hill echoes "aho bilam" (what a wonder!); nine forms of the Lion are worshipped along the forest ridges, and the Ahobila Mutt’s lineage was founded here by the Lord himself as guru.

pasuram.meaning: The wondrous Lion of Ahobilam whose roar still shakes the Nallamala ridges.

ayodhya.puranam: The Sarayu-banked city of Rama’s birth and reign — Thirumangai Azhwar sang it from afar, never leaving Tamil soil, calling its Lord the king whose very name carries the soul across.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar’s northern pilgrimage in verse — Ayodhya, city of the Lord who walked as a king among men.

naimisaranyam.puranam: The sages gathered (naimisha) at this forest where the Puranas were first narrated; the Lord promised to remain here as the forest itself — the wheel-shaped Chakra tirtha marks where his discus rested.

pasuram.meaning: The Lord who made himself the forest-shrine of Naimisaranya where wisdom was first sung.

timings.notes: Himalayan shrine — open only in fair months (approx. May–Oct)

moolavar.name: Moorthy (Muktinath, Sri Murthy)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, with 108 bull-mouth water spouts

salagramam.puranam: At 3,800 metres beneath the Thorong pass, 108 icy springs pour over the devotee for liberation — Muktinath is the shrine of the saligrama stones themselves, honoured by both Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims as Chumig Gyatsa.

pasuram.meaning: Thirumangai’s hymn reaches the Himalayan Salagrama where liberation flows in icy water.

timings.notes: Closed in winter (approx. Oct–Apr); deity moved to Joshimutt

moolavar.name: Badri Narayana (Badri Vishal)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated in padmasana under the badri tree

badari.puranam: Nara and Narayana, the sage-twins, performed tapas here; the berry (badri) grove shielded Narayana from the sun — and the Lord remains seated in yoga at the Alaknanda’s source, the north’s supreme abode of liberation.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwars place Badari and Venkatam as the twin poles of the Lord’s grace on earth.

devaprayag.puranam: Where Alaknanda meets Bhagirathi and the Ganga is born, Rama performed penance after Ravana’s fall at this confluence — the kshetram of the "divine confluence" (deva prayag).

pasuram.meaning: The cloud-hued Lord of the confluence where the Ganga is born of two rivers.

timings.notes: Winter seat of Badrinath

joshimutt.puranam: Adi Sankara established the Jyotirmath seat here; when Badrinath closes under snow, the Lord’s worship continues at this winter throne — the meditation-seat (jyoti) of the Himalaya.

pasuram.meaning: The seated Paramapurusha of Piridi who keeps the lamp of the north alight.

mathura.puranam: Krishna’s birth-city on the Yamuna, praised by Periyazhwar who longed to be born there as anything that breathes — the hill nearby is the very Govardhana the Lord lifted on his finger.

pasuram.meaning: Periyazhwar’s northern verses bless every leaf and stone of Krishna’s Mathura.

timings.notes: Vrindavan-Gokul region shrines

moolavar.name: Navamohana Krishna
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing, the eternally enchanting child

ayarpadi.puranam: The cowherd settlement (aaypadi) of Krishna’s childhood — Vrindavan and Gokul — where the Azhwars’ longing fixates on the enchanter (navamohan) of every soul; Andal’s Thiruppavai borrows its very voice from these groves.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar envies the cows and calves of Ayarpadi that felt the Lord’s touch.

timings.notes: Flag changes five times daily

moolavar.name: Kalyana Narayanan (Dwarakadhish)
moolavar.form: Nindran — standing as the king of Dwaraka

dwaraka.puranam: Krishna’s golden capital on the western sea — the gateway (dwaraka) city that returned to the waters after his age ended; the flag atop the temple has changed five times a day for centuries, as the king keeps his court.

pasuram.meaning: Andal’s longing verses name Dwaraka among the cities of her beloved’s reign.

moolavar.name: Ksheerabdinathan (Ranganatha of the Ocean of Milk)
moolavar.form: Kidandan — reclining on Adisesha amid the milky ocean

thirupparkadal.puranam: Beyond earthly geography, the Ocean of Milk is where every cosmic age finds the Lord reclining in eternal ease — reached not by road or rail but by contemplation; the Azhwars sang it as the thirteenth month’s pilgrimage.

pasuram.meaning: The Azhwar’s verses ferry the soul to the milky ocean where the Lord awaits every age.

moolavar.name: Vaikuntanathan (Paramapadanathan)
moolavar.form: Irundhan — seated in the supreme abode

paramapadam.puranam: The last of the 108 is not a place but the destination — Vaikunta, the supreme abode from which none returns, granted by the Lord’s own grace to the soul that surrenders.

pasuram.meaning: Nammazhwar’s final decad is itself the soul’s departure — the Lord’s abode received as his own.
